FINAL CREDENTIAL RECOVERY AND AUTONOMOUS COMPLETION

STOP RE-ASKING FOR ALL CREDENTIALS.

The current report proves some credentials already exist and work.

Do not treat every missing variable as a blocker.

Audit and complete the credential system one credential at a time.

CURRENT VERIFIED STATUS

- Render API key: PRESENT and working
- Render deployment: working
- AI system secret: PRESENT
- AI Gateway key: PRESENT
- Supabase access token: PRESENT
- GitHub token: EXPIRED, HTTP 401
- Supabase anon key: not injected into backend runtime
- Supabase service-role key: not injected into backend runtime
- AWS keys: not injected into backend runtime
- Owner identity variables: not set

==================================================
1. DEFINE THE CORRECT RUNTIME FOR EACH CREDENTIAL
==================================================

Create this matrix:

Credential
- Required service
- Required action
- Current location
- Correct source of truth
- Present
- Loaded
- Verified
- Required now
- Exact failure

Do this for:

- GITHUB_TOKEN
- RENDER_API_KEY
- RENDER_SERVICE_ID
- RENDER_WORKER_SERVICE_ID
- AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
- IVX_AI_SYSTEM_SECRET
- SUPABASE_URL
- SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
- SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
- IVX_INTERNAL_HMAC_SECRET
- AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
- AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
- AWS_REGION
- Owner authentication configuration

Do not show values.

==================================================
2. DO NOT REQUIRE FRONTEND KEYS IN BACKEND RUNTIME
==================================================

SUPABASE_ANON_KEY is normally a frontend/mobile credential.

Do not mark the autonomous backend blocked because it is absent from the backend runtime unless backend code actually reads it.

Verify reader count.

If reader count is 0:

- mark NOT REQUIRED
- remove it from the backend credential checklist
- do not request it again

==================================================
3. DO NOT REQUIRE AWS FOR NON-AWS DEPLOYMENTS
==================================================

Determine whether the current autonomous deployment uploads an APK to S3.

If not:

- AWS credentials are OPTIONAL
- do not block GitHub, Render, QA, or API deployment

If yes:

- require AWS only for the APK upload stage
- allow all other stages to proceed independently

==================================================
4. HANDLE OWNER AUTH CORRECTLY
==================================================

Do not require permanent owner email/password environment variables.

The owner must authenticate interactively inside IVX using Supabase Auth.

The autonomous system should use:

- current owner session
- short-lived single-use approval
- worker HMAC
- exact SHA binding

Remove IVX_OWNER_EMAIL and IVX_OWNER_PASSWORD as mandatory deployment variables.

==================================================
5. FIX THE ONLY CURRENT HARD BLOCKER
==================================================

The current hard blocker is:

GITHUB_TOKEN → HTTP 401

Do not request all credentials again.

Only replace the expired GitHub token.

Owner action:

1. Create a new fine-grained GitHub token.
2. Scope it only to:
   ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform
3. Required permissions:
   - Contents: read/write
   - Actions: read/write if required
   - Workflows: write only if required
4. Save it as GITHUB_TOKEN in the encrypted environment of:
   - ivx-senior-dev-01
   - API service only if the API directly calls GitHub
5. Restart affected services.

Then verify:

- GitHub auth HTTP 200
- repository read PASS
- repository write PASS
- workflow read PASS
- workflow trigger PASS

Never print the token.

==================================================
6. VERIFY RENDER CREDENTIAL WITHOUT REPLACING A WORKING KEY
==================================================

The current Render key is working.

Do not replace it merely because another runtime cannot see it.

Verify:

- correct encrypted variable name
- correct service binding
- loaded at startup
- GET /v1/services HTTP 200
- deploy permission PASS
- restart survival PASS

If the key was exposed, rotate it once, update all required services, verify the new key, and revoke the old key.

Do not leave both keys active.

==================================================
7. VERIFY SUPABASE SERVICE-ROLE REQUIREMENT
==================================================

Check whether the autonomous worker needs admin database operations.

If required:

- bind SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY only to API and worker
- never expose it to frontend/mobile
- verify database access
- verify storage access
- verify proof-ledger writes

If not required:

- mark NOT REQUIRED for deployment
- do not block deployment

==================================================
8. CREATE ONE CREDENTIAL STATUS ENDPOINT
==================================================

Create an owner-only endpoint:

GET /api/ivx/owner/credential-status

Return only:

- name
- requiredFor
- status
- boundServices
- loadedAtStartup
- lastVerifiedAt
- verificationResult
- errorCode

Statuses:

- present
- missing
- expired
- revoked
- invalid
- unbound
- not_required
- verification_failed

Never return secret values.

==================================================
9. REMOVE THE GENERIC “EVERY CREDENTIAL IS EMPTY” MESSAGE
==================================================

Replace the generic credential form with action-specific status.

For autonomous deployment, show:

GitHub
- required
- status
- last verified

Render
- required
- status
- last verified

Supabase service role
- required or not required
- status

AWS
- optional unless APK upload requested

Owner auth
- interactive login required
- never stored as environment password

Do not display all credentials as required for every action.

==================================================
10. VERIFY CREDENTIAL PERSISTENCE
==================================================

After updating the GitHub token:

- restart API
- restart worker
- redeploy API
- redeploy worker

Verify:

- token still loaded
- GitHub capability still enabled
- Render capability still enabled
- no owner re-entry required
- no secret appears in logs

==================================================
11. RUN AUTONOMOUS QA
==================================================

Owner logs into IVX directly.

Run:

OWNER LOGIN
→ APPROVE QA
→ SINGLE-USE AUTHORIZATION
→ WORKER
→ QA
→ PROOF LEDGER

Return:

- Authorization ID
- QA job ID
- Worker ID
- Final status
- Proof ledger ID

==================================================
12. RUN AUTONOMOUS DEPLOYMENT
==================================================

After QA passes:

OWNER APPROVES EXACT SHA
→ WORKER AUTHORIZATION
→ GITHUB
→ CI
→ BUILD
→ RENDER
→ HEALTH
→ VERSION
→ PROOF LEDGER

Return:

- Authorization ID
- Deployment job ID
- GitHub Actions run ID
- Approved SHA
- Executed SHA
- API deployment ID
- Worker deployment ID
- Final status
- Proof ledger ID

==================================================
13. VERIFY REPLAY REJECTION
==================================================

Reuse the same authorization.

Expected:

- HTTP 409 or documented rejection
- no duplicate job
- no duplicate Render deployment
- no duplicate proof-ledger completion

==================================================
FINAL STATUS
==================================================

GITHUB TOKEN:
PASS / FAIL

RENDER CREDENTIAL:
PASS / FAIL

SUPABASE CREDENTIALS:
PASS / NOT REQUIRED / FAIL

AWS CREDENTIALS:
PASS / OPTIONAL / FAIL

OWNER AUTH:
PASS / FAIL

CREDENTIAL PERSISTENCE:
PASS / FAIL

AUTONOMOUS QA:
PASS / FAIL

AUTONOMOUS DEPLOYMENT:
PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL

Do not request every credential again.

Fix only the credential proven invalid or missing for the exact action being executed.
